title: Why Do Some Sand Dunes Sing?
narration:
What if the ground beneath your feet started singing? In a few deserts on Earth, giant sand dunes do exactly that. They boom, hum and roar so loudly that travelers once blamed spirits. Today we know what is really happening, and the answer is stranger than any legend.

The sound starts when sand slides down the steep face of a dune. Millions of grains move together, and their tiny collisions line up into one deep tone. Some dunes hum at a low note that you can feel in your chest. The sound can last for minutes and be heard far across the desert.

So why do only some dunes sing? Scientists found that the grains must be dry, rounded and similar in size, and the dune must be steep enough to avalanche. When everything lines up, the desert becomes an instrument. Subscribe for a new midnight question.
